links_touching_record.rationale: FB2-SW-SIR-000003 is the software interface requirement set for the communication and data exchange boundary and is specified by FB2-SW-IFS-000004 (CAN transport) and FB2-SW-IFS-000005 (database engine). The direction is specification to requirement, which is the direction a requirement is written in: the interface specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source at the pinned commit, and the requirement states what must be true of it. This is the opposite of the direction the three existing FB2-SW-SWR-* requirements were produced in - those are back-inferred from the implementation and their revision history says so - and naming the relationship explicitly is what keeps the two directions distinguishable. Every statement in the requirement is traceable to a named element of the specification, and the requirement carries that traceability as a field rather than leaving it in prose.

The second specification FB2-SW-SIR-000003 is derived from. FB2-SW-SIR-000003 covers the communication and data exchange boundary and its derivation field names every interface specification it came from; this link names the second one so that a reader following the requirement to its evidence reaches both specifications rather than only the first. The direction and the reason are the same as for the first specification: the specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source, and the requirement states what must be true of it.

The triage record classifies the disposition of element FB2-SW-SIR-000003-B, which the communication interface-requirement record states and marks NOT SATISFIED. Same dependency direction as the actuation triage: the disposition rests on the requirement record's element statement and is re-read against the source rather than trusted from the status field.

asil_justification.statement: Not applicable, and deliberately so. This requirement carries no safety allocation because the item it describes has not been through a hazard analysis and risk assessment, so there is no severity or exposure rating to derive an ASIL from. No ASIL is asserted for the real product and none is asserted here. This is not a statement that the interface is unimportant: it is a statement that the classification apparatus is not available in this repository, and a reader must not read 'not_applicable' as 'no consequence'.

authority_and_independence.independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent. It is a derivation from an analysed specification, not an elicitation, not an analysis of a higher-level requirement, and not independent review.

derivation.authoring_independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent from the interface specifications and the source. No requirements engineer confirmed that this is the interface that was wanted, no stakeholder stated a need that these requirements answer, and no human approved them. They record what the code obliges a consumer to rely on; they do not record what anyone asked for.
derivation.method: Every statement below names the interface element it obliges and the analysed behaviour it rests on.

element_requirements.basis: STD_OK is assigned only inside the message-box loop after the transmit call; the initial negative value is returned when the loop finds no free box.
element_requirements.statement: A transmit call shall report whether the frame was placed on a free message box.

element_requirements.basis: NOT satisfied by the analysed implementation. The source records the absence of a check as a deliberate decision and shifts the value into the controller register with no mask.
element_requirements.statement: The identifier argument shall be bounded by the identifier width the caller selected, and an identifier wider than that width shall be rejected.

element_requirements.basis: The public element only enqueues; the copy is performed later on the consumer task. The return value is the enqueue result.
element_requirements.statement: The data-block read shall report whether the request was accepted, and shall not be represented as returning the data.

element_requirements.basis: The queue send is given a timeout computed from a declared 10 ms maximum, statically asserted to be non-zero.
element_requirements.statement: The data-block read shall bound the time a caller waits to enqueue its request.

element_requirements.basis: All access is routed through one queue and one consumer drains it, which is what serialises concurrent access.
element_requirements.statement: Concurrent access to the data blocks shall be serialised through a single consumer of the database queue.

record_verbatim.element_requirements_note: The failure reaction of these two boundaries is the reason most of this set is unsatisfied. On the communication side a refused transmit is reported but a congested queue is not: when a queued frame cannot be re-queued the branch body is empty apart from a comment, so the frame is discarded with no return value, no diagnosis event and no log. On the data-exchange side a caller that is refused its enqueue gets a negative value but no byte count and no indication that a previously accepted request may now be stale. Neither failure has a detection channel.
record_verbatim.failure_reaction: Two of these five are not satisfied by the implementation as analysed, and the other three are. The unsatisfied pair is the interesting one: B has no bound and no rejection, and the transmit queue discards a frame with no return value, no diagnosis event and no log when the retransmit queue is full. Together they mean the communication boundary has no defined failure behaviour for either an over-wide identifier or a congested bus. Stating them as requirements is what makes that actionable rather than incidental.
not_established_by_this_record: Requirements B and the queue-discard behaviour are not satisfied by the implementation as analysed. B would need either a range check on the identifier or a mask on the shift; the queue-discard behaviour would need a defined drop path with a signal. Neither exists and this record does not claim otherwise.
No requirement here is elicited from a stakeholder, a system requirement or a safety goal.

The requirement set states no bus-level contract: no bit rate, no identifier allocation, no maximum frame rate, no maximum payload length. The bit rate is configuration and the identifier allocation is spread across the transmit callback files, neither of which is named by the analysed interfaces.
The requirement set states no coherency or atomicity rule for a multi-entry data-block read, so nothing here can be used to justify a requirement that a group of values be mutually consistent.
No ASIL, no safety allocation, no conformity claim, no certification, no human approval.
No verification has been performed against any of these requirements and no test measure exists for any of them.
record_verbatim.rationale: These requirements exist because the two analysed boundaries behave differently in ways a consumer must know and cannot infer from a signature. The transmit interface has an explicitly unchecked identifier, recorded in the source as a deliberate non-assert, and its queue pump discards a frame when the retransmit queue is full. The data-exchange interface is asynchronous: it returns before the data exists, and its return value reports only whether the request was queued. A consumer of either would have to read the implementation to learn that, which is the situation an interface requirement exists to prevent.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Five interface requirements over the communication and data-exchange boundaries, derived from FB2-SW-IFS-000004 and FB2-SW-IFS-000005. Two of them are stated because the analysed interface does not satisfy them, and that is the point of writing them down.

safety_allocation.mitigation: No ASIL is allocated to this requirement. It is a software interface requirement about how two modules call each other, and the product it describes has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment: no ISO 26262 conformity, no ASIL determination and no certification is claimed for it or for anything in this corpus. The non-applicability is stated with its reason rather than left blank, because an unexplained non-applicability is indistinguishable from a requirement that quietly dropped out of every ASIL-derived view.

standards_mappings.rationale: Supplies software interface requirements, the family SWE.1 expected and that was absent. It does not analyse them from a higher-level requirement, so the process's defining activity is still absent.

Backs SWE.1 with the software interface requirement family. The status stays partially_mapped because these requirements are derived from an analysis of an existing implementation, not analysed from software requirements or system requirements, and because the existing software requirements remain back-inferred.

Consumes the interface specifications this requirement set is derived from. A requirement derived from a specification is the direction that makes the specification the engineering content and this the obligation.

record_verbatim.statement: The communication and data-exchange interfaces shall present the following to their consumers: (a) a transmit call whose result reports whether the frame was placed on the bus; (b) an identifier argument whose range is bounded by the identifier width the caller selected; (c) a data-block read whose result reports whether the request was accepted and which shall not be represented as returning the data; (d) a bounded maximum queue wait on that read; and (e) a single-consumer serialisation rule for concurrent access to the data blocks.
record_verbatim.title: Software interface requirements: the communication and data-exchange interfaces

verification_status.statement: No test measure exists for any requirement in this record, and no requirement in it has been verified against running code. Every derivation below is an inspection of the source at the pinned commit, which is why the verification approach is analysis and why the coverage matrix in the implementation mapping document reports this record as uncovered. That is the accurate position, not a gap to be filled by writing more prose.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-SW-SIR-000003` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/ or docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record
6. a revision_history entry whose author is the approving role and whose description records the approval and cites the signed packet

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.

target.primary_key_rule: ID-RULE-004-A1: an artefact identifier is unique within its profile; two records of different profiles may carry the same identifier string.
